names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 20 aprilie, «Sfântul Cuvios Anastasie Sinaitul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Αναστάσιος ο Σιναΐτης», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 20. април ст. ст., „Преп. Анастасије Синајски.“, with the rank word Преп. left off. The by-name Синајски is kept: it is not a rank, it is what the heading gives beyond the forename, and `anastasius-the-persian` already holds the bare «Анастасије», which a bare form here would fold onto. The Prologue's next entry calls the patriarch of Antioch Синаит, so the book itself spells the two by-names apart.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 20 апреля ст. ст., name page 6606, «Анастасий, игумен Синайской горы, прп.», with the grade прп. left off. The descriptive phrase is kept, comma and all, on the corpus’s own pattern for «Аммон, затворник Печерский» and «Алексий, человек Божий»: the bare forename is a wide fold, and the epithet Синаит which the page gives him in its body is the one the patriarch of the same name is stored under two entries above. Measured against the gate’s own key function before it was written: 'анастасии горы игумен синаискои' has no other holder.

birth.note: doxologia.ro: «Sfântul Anastasie s-a născut la Alexandria, în Egipt în prima jumătate a secolului al VII-lea».

death.note: Two sources disagree and neither is displaced. doxologia.ro: «A trecut la Domnul cu pace, la adânci bătrânețe, cândva după anul 700». The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 20 April: „Скончао у дубокој старости 685. год. и отишао ка Господу, коме је верно послужио.“ Both have him die in deep old age, and the Prologue's year falls below the lower bound doxologia gives, so the interval was widened to hold both readings rather than either of them narrowed away: the earliest is the Prologue's 685 and the upper bound stays open, as doxologia's «după anul 700» leaves it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 20 апреля ст. ст. — «Прп. Анастасия , игумена Синайской горы (695).»
source.note: A separate entry from the patriarch of the same name and the same surname two lines above, with its own name page (6606) and its own life page (life903). The name page gives «День памяти: 20 апреля» and no other day. ONE DISAGREEMENT LEFT UNRESOLVED: this life opens «родился в конце VI века», born at the end of the sixth century, while the birth interval on this folder is doxologia.ro’s «în prima jumătate a secolului al VII-lea», the first half of the seventh, at Alexandria. The Russian names no birthplace at all. A year is not this reader’s to decide and `dates` was not changed. The day page prints no hymn under his name.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 20 aprilie — «Sfântul Cuvios Anastasie Sinaitul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Απριλίου — «Όσιος Αναστάσιος ο Σιναΐτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him. That answers a question the day before raised: saint.gr's 20 Απριλίου lists only «Άγιος Αναστάσιος Ιερομάρτυρας, επίσκοπος Αντιοχείας», so the Sinaite's Greek day is this one and not that. The page agrees with the years this folder already holds and does not sharpen them: «έζησε τον 7ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» and «Αφού έφτασε σε βαθιά γεράματα, απεβίωσε ειρηνικά στις αρχές του 8ου αιώνος μ.Χ.», so the `dates` were left untouched. It adds that he was of a noble family, that he went as a pilgrim to Jerusalem and ended at Sinai in the monastery of St Catherine, of which he was abbot, that he stayed there among the ascetics as their subordinate and servant, and that for his humility he received from God the gift of knowledge and much wisdom, with which he wrote lives of holy fathers and composed soul-profiting discourses. It then lists six of his works by title and quotes a passage of his on not judging. It prints no hymn and names no relic.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.05.2026 (20. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Анастасије Синајски.“
